task.description: STRATEGY CHANGE required for GH #566 / ISS-0617. The previously-validated migration approach (GBL-136, already implemented and merged into this run's history at migrations/GBL-136_iss0617_drop_remaining_global_registry_shadows.sql) cannot achieve the actual goal for repository_artifacts, the direct root cause table. Confirmed via live pg_constraint query on both bpm_dev and bpm_test: tenant_default.artifact_versions has FK fk_artifact_versions_content (ON DELETE RESTRICT) pointing INTO tenant_default.repository_artifacts. Since artifact_versions itself can NEVER be dropped (permanent FK dependents from legitimate PER_TENANT tables artifact_activations, artifact_activation_history, repository_form_schemas -- already documented in the GBL-136 design), it PERMANENTLY, TRANSITIVELY blocks repository_artifacts from ever being dropped via RESTRICT too. This is not fixable by reordering the migration's table list or any other migration-level tweak -- it is a structural impossibility as long as artifact_versions exists in tenant_default. Verified empirically: GBL-136 was applied cleanly to both bpm_dev and bpm_test (6 of 8 target tables dropped successfully, exactly as expected; repository_artifacts and artifact_versions both remain, only artifact_versions was anticipated to remain). NEW RECOMMENDED STRATEGY (from BACKEND-DEV's investigation, needs your design review before implementation): the actual proximate cause per ISS-0617's confirmed_root_cause is tests/integration/exp601_tier_quota_test.zig:53's unqualified `INSERT INTO repository_artifacts` resolving via TestHarness's search_path=tenant_default,public to the wrong (stray, permanently un-droppable) shadow copy, instead of public.repository_artifacts, which is what src/config/loader.zig's loadConfigArtifact (search_path=public only) actually queries. Schema-qualifying this test fixture's INSERT (and any other unqualified repository_artifacts references in this test file -- check tests/integration/exp601_tier_quota_test.zig in full for all of them, there may be more than the one at line 53) to explicitly target public.repository_artifacts would fix TC-EXP-601-01 through 04 directly, without requiring any DROP TABLE at all. This is a test-file-only fix, much smaller and safer than the migration approach. Design this properly: confirm every repository_artifacts reference in the test file, confirm qualifying to public. is correct and doesn't break anything else the test relies on, and confirm this approach doesn't need the GBL-136 migration at all for THIS specific issue (GBL-136 may still be worth keeping/shipping for its other 6 tables' cleanup, that's a separate question from whether it's REQUIRED for GH-566).
acceptance_criteria: Every unqualified repository_artifacts reference in tests/integration/exp601_tier_quota_test.zig identified
Design specifies schema-qualifying these references to public.repository_artifacts
Design confirms this satisfies TC-EXP-601-01 through 04 without requiring repository_artifacts to ever be dropped from tenant_default
Design states explicitly whether GBL-136 (already implemented, covers the other 6 tables) should still ship alongside this fix or be reverted -- with reasoning
No implementation code present in the design artefact
